claims.text: Static EAM references inadequately represent the diverse atomic configurations of ab initio liquid states.
An active-learning neural-network potential will capture the diverse configurations of ab initio alloy liquids more accurately than static EAM references.
Replacing EAM references with an active-learning neural-network potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Replacing EAM references with an active-learning neural-network potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The neural-network potential should be trained iteratively on ab initio configurations from both solid and liquid alloy phases.
The proposed neural-network architecture can incorporate many-body interactions and thermal fluctuations.
Representing many-body interactions and thermal fluctuations allows the potential to adapt to diverse local liquid configurations.
Active learning updates the potential's training set with newly selected ab initio data.
Iterative inclusion of ab initio configurations expands the phase space covered by the reference potential.
Expanded training coverage produces a more accurate model of the alloy energy landscape.
A more accurate energy landscape reduces mismatch along thermodynamic-integration paths.
The intervention will improve the accuracy of computed free energies relative to TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references.
The intervention is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in equilibrium solid and liquid states at or near their high melting temperatures.
The intervention may be less effective in systems with extreme short-range order.
The intervention may be less effective for systems far from equilibrium.
The magnitude of the reduction in path mismatch may vary with alloy composition and temperature.
